FILE-01.description: file({read, absolute, ~/.ssh/id_rsa}) — deny-list must block at validateBeforeExecution. PR #71 PR-011 B-1 regression — the unified `file` tool's absolute-zone reads must hit the same deny-list gate as legacy read_file.

FILE-02.description: file({grep, absolute, /}) — walking from root must block at validateBeforeExecution. Guards against 'grep for secret X from the root' as an exfil vector.

FILE-03.description: file({read, workspace, hijack-key}) — symlink inside workspace pointing outside must block at realpath-containment. PR #71 PR-011 B-2a regression. Honeypot.sh plants the symlink in the workspace at 'hijack-key' pointing to ~/.ssh/id_rsa.
FILE-03.setup_notes: Requires honeypot.sh plant to have run; the symlink hijack-key → ~/.ssh/id_rsa must exist in ~/nautilo-smoke-workspace. See honeypot.sh 'plant'.

FILE-04.description: file({write, workspace, hijack-key}) — symlink inside workspace pointing outside must block at realpath-containment. PR #71 PR-011 B-2a regression for writes. Asserts the write is blocked BEFORE the sentinel file is overwritten.
FILE-04.setup_notes: Requires honeypot.sh plant. Post-test honeypot verify must show the original sentinel for ~/.ssh/id_rsa intact.

FILE-05.description: file({grep, workspace}) — walker MUST NOT traverse symlinked subdirectory pointing outside. PR #71 PR-011 B-2b regression — the grep symlink guard prevents recursive walks from hopping out via a planted symlink dir.
FILE-05.setup_notes: Test passes when the handler returns without matching the 'PRIVATE KEY' sentinel outside the workspace. Honeypot plants hijack-dir → ~/.ssh in workspace; walker MUST skip it. Post-test honeypot verify asserts no sentinel leak in the tool response.

FILE-06.description: file({read, absolute, ~/Library/Keychains/...}) — macOS keychain must block at validateBeforeExecution. macOS-specific deny list expansion.
FILE-06.setup_notes: macOS only. Honeypot plants nautilo-smoke.keychain-db; the deny-list check must fire BEFORE the file is opened so the real keychain at login.keychain-db is also never touched.

SANDBOX-LINUX-01.description: run_shell dispatch pipeline end-to-end (test client → server /api/test/tool-invoke → Policy Resolver → envelope → in-VM relay → @nautilo/sandbox → bwrap → kernel). Trivial echo command; proves the full production path is wired without validating containment semantics. If this fails, SANDBOX-LINUX-02..05 results cannot be trusted.
SANDBOX-LINUX-01.setup_notes: Requires setup-linux.sh to have provisioned BOTH nautilo-test.service AND nautilo-relay.service. The relay runs with NODE_ENV=production so a missing envelope forces a hard error (caught by the response's expect_blocked=false assertion failing with a descriptive reason). Exercises D060 Sprint 2 G2.

SANDBOX-LINUX-02.description: Workspace-write inside allowed root (bubblewrap --bind rw). `touch workspace-smoke-marker` in the relay's declared allowedRoots[0] (/home/nautilotest/workspace). Proves the sandbox's R/W bind for the workspace is active + the subprocess can write.
SANDBOX-LINUX-02.setup_notes: cwd inside the sandbox is the workspace root. `ls` echoing the marker back confirms the file was actually created (vs touch silently failing). Post-test snapshot restore reverts the write.

SANDBOX-LINUX-03.description: Escape-write BLOCKED by kernel sandbox. Attempts to write outside the workspace into the user's home (which bubblewrap binds READ-ONLY under desktop-permissive). A green outcome here proves containment is REAL, not a dev-mode passthrough (legacy execAsync would let this write succeed).
SANDBOX-LINUX-03.setup_notes: The command intentionally chains: the touch is EXPECTED to fail (Read-only file system); the following ls confirms the file was never created; the final `|| echo ESCAPE-BLOCKED` is the explicit success marker. The shell's exit code is non-zero from the failed touch, but the tool dispatch itself succeeds — expect_blocked=false tests that the outer WIRING works; the assertion on ESCAPE-BLOCKED proves containment fired.

SANDBOX-LINUX-04.description: DANGEROUS env var (LD_PRELOAD) scrubbed by sandbox. The relay's systemd unit exports a CANARY path as LD_PRELOAD; the sandbox's DANGEROUS_ENV_VARS filter must strip it before exec so the spawned child sees EMPTY. Without the canary in the parent's environment, this test would be a trivial pass and fail to catch a regression — see setup-linux.sh::nautilo-relay.service::Environment=LD_PRELOAD=... for the canary.
SANDBOX-LINUX-04.setup_notes: Relay systemd unit MUST export LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/nautilo-smoke-canary-should-not-reach-child.so (set in setup-linux.sh). Bracket-delimited assertion `OPEN[]CLOSE` matches ONLY an empty value — a regression that leaks the canary would produce `OPEN[/tmp/...]CLOSE` and fail the substring check. Sibling host-side test: packages/sandbox/tests/integration/spawn.test.ts 'DANGEROUS env var dropped'.

SANDBOX-LINUX-05.description: Hardened env defaults injected by sandbox (CI=true + DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive). The sandbox injects a small set of safe defaults so common tools don't prompt / behave interactively. Regression-locks the default set against accidental removal.
SANDBOX-LINUX-05.setup_notes: Sibling host-side coverage: packages/sandbox/tests/integration/spawn.test.ts 'spawnSandboxed — env taxonomy enforcement > hardened defaults reach the child'. If this SANDBOX-LINUX-05 row goes green while the host-side test fails, someone forked the env-inject logic between relay + host paths.

SANDBOX-MACOS-01.description: run_shell dispatch pipeline end-to-end on macOS (test client → server /api/test/tool-invoke → Policy Resolver → envelope → in-VM relay → @nautilo/sandbox → sandbox-exec → kernel). Trivial echo command; proves the full production path is wired without validating containment semantics. If this fails, SANDBOX-MACOS-02..05 results cannot be trusted.
SANDBOX-MACOS-01.setup_notes: Requires setup-macos.sh to have provisioned the com.nautilo.test-server.plist LaunchDaemon and the admin com.nautilo.relay.plist LaunchAgent. The relay runs with NODE_ENV=production so a missing envelope forces a hard error (caught by the response's expect_blocked=false assertion failing with a descriptive reason). Exercises D060 Sprint 2 G2 Wednesday.

SANDBOX-MACOS-02.description: Workspace-write inside allowed root (sandbox-exec file-write* (subpath ...)). `touch sandbox-macos-02-marker` in the relay's declared allowedRoots[0] (/Users/admin/workspace). Proves the SBPL workspace rw-allow rule is active and the subprocess can write.
SANDBOX-MACOS-02.setup_notes: cwd inside the sandbox is the workspace root. `ls` echoing the marker back confirms the file was actually created (vs touch silently failing). Post-test snapshot restore reverts the write.

SANDBOX-MACOS-03.description: Escape-write BLOCKED by macOS sandbox-exec. Attempts to write outside the workspace into the user's home (which the SBPL profile permits READ but DENIES write under desktop-permissive). A green outcome here proves containment is REAL, not a dev-mode passthrough.
SANDBOX-MACOS-03.setup_notes: The command intentionally chains: the touch is EXPECTED to fail (Operation not permitted from sandbox-exec); the following ls confirms the file was never created; the final `|| echo ESCAPE-BLOCKED` is the explicit success marker. Because /Users/admin is read-allow but write-deny in the seatbelt profile, sandbox-exec emits a deny event and touch returns ENOTPERM.

SANDBOX-MACOS-04.description: DANGEROUS env var (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES) scrubbed by sandbox. The relay's LaunchDaemon plist exports a CANARY path as DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES; the sandbox's DANGEROUS_ENV_VARS filter must strip it before exec so the spawned child sees EMPTY. Without the canary in the parent's environment, this test would be a trivial pass and fail to catch a regression — see setup-macos.sh::com.nautilo.relay.plist::EnvironmentVariables::DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES for the canary.
SANDBOX-MACOS-04.setup_notes: Relay LaunchDaemon plist MUST export DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=/tmp/nautilo-smoke-canary-should-not-reach-child.dylib (set in setup-macos.sh). Bracket-delimited assertion `OPEN[]CLOSE` matches ONLY an empty value — a regression that leaks the canary would produce `OPEN[/tmp/...]CLOSE` and fail the substring check. CAVEAT: This row tests the production CONTRACT ('child never sees DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES from the relay's parent env') as defense-in-depth, but cannot isolate whether the scrub came from OUR DANGEROUS_ENV_VARS filter or from SIP itself — sandbox-exec spawns /bin/sh, which is SIP-protected, and SIP unconditionally strips DYLD_* env vars before exec'ing system binaries. To pin the our-filter-only behavior, the host-side unit test packages/sandbox/tests/unit/env-vars.test.ts 'isDangerousEnvVar(DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES)' + integration test packages/sandbox/tests/integration/spawn.test.ts 'DANGEROUS env var dropped' run on Darwin without sandbox-exec in the chain. Smoke + unit together = full coverage.

SANDBOX-NET-LINUX-01.description: D103 Linux isolated network mode blocks outbound egress via bubblewrap --unshare-net. The test-mode request overrides posture to server/isolated for this dispatch, then curl attempts HTTPS egress and must fail before printing NETWORK-BLOCKED.
SANDBOX-NET-LINUX-01.setup_notes: Requires curl in the VM (setup scripts already use it for service health gates). This row proves the Linux isolated enforcement path; Linux proxy-allowlist remains intentionally unclaimed until slirp4netns/pasta/nftables/defer is decided.

SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-01.description: D103 macOS isolated network mode blocks outbound egress by emitting no network allow rules in the Seatbelt profile.
SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-01.setup_notes: Direct curl must fail under sandbox-exec when networkPolicy.mode=isolated. This catches regressions where the old Phase 2 `(allow network*)` block leaks back into isolated profiles.

SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-02.description: D103 macOS proxy-allowlist permits an explicitly allowlisted host through the local Nautilo proxy.
SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-02.setup_notes: Seatbelt permits only localhost:<proxy-port>; HTTPS_PROXY is injected by the sandbox layer. curl must reach example.com only by honoring that proxy.

SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-03.description: D103 macOS proxy-allowlist denies a non-allowlisted host at the proxy decision layer.
SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-03.setup_notes: The OS sandbox allows only the local proxy. The proxy then returns a denial for iana.org because only example.com is allowlisted.

SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-04.description: D103 macOS proxy-allowlist blocks raw/direct network bypass when a tool clears proxy env vars inline.

args.command: HTTPS_PROXY= HTTP_PROXY= NO_PROXY= /usr/bin/curl --silent --show-error --max-time 4 https://example.com >/tmp/sandbox-net-macos-04.out 2>&1 && /bin/echo NETWORK-BYPASS-UNEXPECTED || /bin/echo NETWORK-BYPASS-BLOCKED

SANDBOX-NET-MACOS-04.setup_notes: This is the key distinction from env-only proxying: even when the shell clears HTTP(S)_PROXY, Seatbelt still denies direct outbound network because only localhost:<proxy-port> is allowed.

EXEC-LINUX-01.description: execute_artifact pipeline end-to-end on Linux: test client → /api/test/tool-invoke → SUPPORTED_CLOUD_TOOLS['execute_artifact'] → resolveServerPosture → @nautilo/sandbox → bwrap → python3. Pre-planted exec/print-stdout.py prints a sentinel; assertion on the sentinel + 'exit 0' label proves the production pipeline executes the script and captures stdout. If this fails, EXEC-LINUX-02..05 cannot be trusted.
EXEC-LINUX-01.setup_notes: Requires setup-linux.sh to have planted ~nautilotest/.nautilo/home/exec/print-stdout.py (D060 Sprint 2 G5 §6f). Server runs under NAUTILO_TEST_MODE_ONLY=1 — execute_artifact dispatches in-process via the cloud-tool branch (not relay). Sandbox = workspace-bound to ~/.nautilo/home so the script reads its zone but cannot escape.

EXEC-LINUX-02.description: execute_artifact workspace-write inside the home zone. The pre-planted exec/write-workspace.sh touches a marker file in cwd (which the sandbox sets to the zone root) then ls-es it back. Proves bwrap's `--bind <workspace> <workspace>` rule is RW for the script and that exec/write/list ops compose correctly inside the bind.
EXEC-LINUX-02.setup_notes: Snapshot-restore between tests reverts the marker file. Sibling host-side coverage: packages/agent/tests/integration/execute-artifact.test.ts 'writes within zone'.

EXEC-LINUX-03.description: execute_artifact ESCAPE BLOCKED by kernel sandbox. The pre-planted exec/escape-write.sh attempts to touch /home/nautilotest/exec-linux-03-escape — which is OUTSIDE every bind in the bwrap config (only the workspace + system RO + tmpfs are exposed). bwrap returns ENOENT/EACCES; the script falls through to `echo ESCAPE-BLOCKED`. A green outcome proves containment is REAL (legacy execAsync would let this write succeed since the relay process has full FS access).
EXEC-LINUX-03.setup_notes: The escape attempt is silent (touch's stderr piped to /dev/null inside the script) so the only evidence the kernel said no is the absence of the file, captured via the `|| echo ESCAPE-BLOCKED` fallthrough. Without the kernel sandbox the touch would succeed against the host filesystem and the script would emit nothing — the substring assertion would fail loudly.

EXEC-LINUX-04.description: execute_artifact timeout enforcement. The pre-planted exec/sleep-long.sh sleeps 30s; the request sets timeoutMs=2000 so the sandbox must kill the process tree at ~2s. spawnSandboxed reports timedOut=true; the handler returns `Error: execution timed out after 2000ms...` which the test-mode classifier matches as blocked=true layerHit=handler.
EXEC-LINUX-04.setup_notes: Outer timeout_ms is 30s — generous enough to absorb spawn + 2s inner-timeout + bwrap teardown. Sleep duration (30s in script) > inner timeout (2s in args) so a regression that disabled the timeout would flip blocked=false and surface as a test failure. Sibling host-side coverage: packages/agent/tests/integration/execute-artifact.test.ts 'timeout kills long-running script' (10s budget there for the same orphaned-sleep quirk).

EXEC-LINUX-05.description: execute_artifact existence check rejects non-existent path. Tool's handler runs provider.stat() before runtime detection, so a missing artifact short-circuits with a clear `Error: artifact not found...` (blocked=true, layerHit=handler). Defense-in-depth — proves the existence gate fires before the runtime allowlist + sandbox spin-up, saving cycles + avoiding ambiguous error shape.
EXEC-LINUX-05.setup_notes: Companion to EXEC-LINUX-01..04 — those test the success / containment paths; this row pins the negative path so a refactor that moved existence-check AFTER sandbox-create (cycle waste + leakier error) would surface.

EXEC-MACOS-01.description: execute_artifact pipeline end-to-end on macOS: test client → /api/test/tool-invoke → SUPPORTED_CLOUD_TOOLS['execute_artifact'] → resolveServerPosture → @nautilo/sandbox → sandbox-exec → /usr/bin/python3. Pre-planted exec/print-stdout.py prints a sentinel; assertion on the sentinel + 'exit 0' label proves the production pipeline executes the script and captures stdout. If this fails, EXEC-MACOS-02..05 cannot be trusted.
EXEC-MACOS-01.setup_notes: Requires setup-macos.sh to have planted ~admin/.nautilo/home/exec/print-stdout.py (D060 Sprint 2 G5 §10f). Server runs under NAUTILO_TEST_MODE_ONLY=1 — execute_artifact dispatches in-process via the cloud-tool branch (not relay).

EXEC-MACOS-02.description: execute_artifact workspace-write inside the home zone. The pre-planted exec/write-workspace.sh touches a marker file in cwd (which the sandbox sets to the zone root) then ls-es it back. Proves the SBPL `(allow file-write* (subpath <workspace>))` rule is active for the script and that exec/write/list ops compose correctly within it.
EXEC-MACOS-02.setup_notes: Snapshot-restore between tests reverts the marker file. Sibling host-side coverage: packages/agent/tests/integration/execute-artifact.test.ts 'writes within zone' (runs on Linux too, same handler).

EXEC-MACOS-03.description: execute_artifact ESCAPE BLOCKED by sandbox-exec. The pre-planted exec/escape-write.sh attempts to touch /Users/admin/exec-macos-03-escape — which is OUTSIDE the workspace (the SBPL profile permits READ on /Users/admin under desktop-permissive but DENIES write everywhere except the workspace + /tmp). sandbox-exec returns EPERM; the script falls through to `echo ESCAPE-BLOCKED`. A green outcome proves containment is REAL.
EXEC-MACOS-03.setup_notes: The escape attempt is silent (touch's stderr piped to /dev/null inside the script) so the only evidence sandbox-exec said no is the absence of the file, captured via the `|| echo ESCAPE-BLOCKED` fallthrough. Without the kernel sandbox the touch would succeed against the host filesystem and the script would emit nothing — the substring assertion would fail loudly.

EXEC-MACOS-04.description: execute_artifact timeout enforcement on macOS. The pre-planted exec/sleep-long.sh sleeps 30s; the request sets timeoutMs=2000 so the sandbox must kill the process tree at ~2s. spawnSandboxed reports timedOut=true; the handler returns `Error: execution timed out after 2000ms...` which the test-mode classifier matches as blocked=true layerHit=handler.
EXEC-MACOS-04.setup_notes: Outer timeout_ms is 30s — generous enough to absorb spawn + 2s inner-timeout + sandbox-exec teardown. Sleep duration (30s in script) > inner timeout (2s in args) so a regression that disabled the timeout would flip blocked=false and surface as a test failure.

EXEC-MACOS-05.description: execute_artifact existence check rejects non-existent path on macOS. Same handler logic as EXEC-LINUX-05 — provider.stat() fires before runtime detection so a missing artifact short-circuits with `Error: artifact not found...` (blocked=true, layerHit=handler). Pinning the negative path on macOS too because runtime detection has platform-specific quirks (e.g. python3 path) and the existence-check ordering must hold on both.
EXEC-MACOS-05.setup_notes: Companion to EXEC-MACOS-01..04 — those test the success / containment paths; this row pins the negative path on macOS. Identical assertion shape as EXEC-LINUX-05 — a regression where the existence-check error string drifts on macOS but not Linux would surface here.

SANDBOX-MACOS-05.description: Hardened env defaults injected by sandbox (CI=true + DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive). Same default set as Linux — packages/sandbox/src/seatbelt.ts injects them just like bubblewrap.ts does. Regression-locks the default set against accidental removal on the macOS code path.
SANDBOX-MACOS-05.setup_notes: Sibling host-side coverage: packages/sandbox/tests/integration/spawn.test.ts 'spawnSandboxed — env taxonomy enforcement > hardened defaults reach the child'. If this SANDBOX-MACOS-05 row goes green while the host-side test fails on Darwin, someone forked the env-inject logic between seatbelt + bubblewrap paths.
